title: Counit normalization and resolution/refinement naturality of the Cech augmentation
statement:
Let $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ be topoi presented by small sites in fixed larger coefficient universes [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], with sheaves of commutative rings $R_X,R_Y$ and module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $f:(\mathcal X,R_X)\to(\mathcal Y,R_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] with Cartesian coefficient identification and exact module inverse image. Let $V\to1_{\mathcal X}$ be an epimorphism of sheaves of sets, $V_n=V^{\times(n+1)}$, and $v_n:\mathcal X/V_n\to\mathcal X$ the slice localizations with rings $v_n^*R_X$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site, def-sfb-element-site-localization, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction]. All diagrams are small. Use ordinary unbounded module derived categories with localization functor $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and finite-diagonal total complexes with differential $d_{\mathrm{Cech}}+(-1)^n d_I$ in Cech degree $n$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Let $a:K[0]\to I$ and $c:L[0]\to J$ be nonnegative injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For any such $I$ set $B_V(I)^{n,q}=(fv_n)_*v_n^*I^q$ with the canonical coherent element-site restrictions [def-sfb-coherent-cech-image-model], and let $b_{V,I}:f_*I\to\operatorname{Tot}B_V(I)$ be the localization-unit augmentation into $(0,q)$. Write $e_I:Q(f_*I)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*(K[0])$ for the canonical resolution comparison and define
$$\alpha_{V,K,I}=Q(b_{V,I})e_I^{-1}:Rf_*(K[0])\longrightarrow Q(\operatorname{Tot}B_V(I)).$$
For every $u:K\to L$ there exists a chain lift $t:I\to J$ of $u$. Every such lift induces a map $\operatorname{Tot}B_V(t)$ satisfying
$$Q(\operatorname{Tot}B_V(t))\alpha_{V,K,I}=\alpha_{V,L,J}Rf_*(u[0]).$$
This map in the derived category is independent of the lift. More explicitly, any chain homotopy $s:t_0\simeq t_1$ gives a total homotopy whose $(n,q)$ component is $(-1)^n(fv_n)_*v_n^*(s^q)$. Comparisons for the identity on $K$ are isomorphisms on the total derived objects, obey identity and composition, and identify the displayed augmentation for all resolutions. For every epimorphism $V'\to1_{\mathcal X}$ and refinement $r:V'\to V$ over $1$, the actual restrictions on fibre powers induce $\rho_r:\operatorname{Tot}B_V(I)\to\operatorname{Tot}B_{V'}(I)$ and
$$Q(\rho_r)\alpha_{V,K,I}=\alpha_{V',K,I};$$
these restrictions obey identities and composition and commute with resolution comparisons. Finally the Cech-degree-zero map is $f_*(\eta_I):f_*I\to f_*v_{0*}v_0^*I$, where $\eta_I:I\to v_{0*}v_0^*I$ is restriction of sections along $v_0$. Before applying $f_*$, the adjoint transpose of $\eta_I$ under $v_0^*\dashv v_{0*}$ is the identity on $v_0^*I$, and evaluation on the slice is the direct-image counit: termwise it satisfies $\varepsilon_{v_0^*I}\,v_0^*\eta_I=\mathrm{id}$. In the derived adjunction $v_0^*\dashv Rv_{0*}$ the unit and counit have these termwise representatives after the canonical right-derived comparisons; hence the same normalization holds for the Cech-degree-zero component of $\alpha_{V,K,I}$ under the displayed resolution comparisons. Here the total map is projected to its degree-zero Cech column before making this assertion.

proof.text: Construct the unique chain augmentation from its prescribed components: use the coherent augmentation into the (0,q) summand. The two degree-zero cofaces have equal composites with the unit, so their alternating sum vanishes. The total differential on column zero therefore gives the chain-map identity. Nonnegative complexes of injectives extend to K-injective complexes by Mathlib. The source right-derived unit and mapExtendIso give exactly the comparison isomorphism in the statement; the separate Cech injective-column model is unnecessary.

source.place: Tags 04IE/04J4; explicit augmentation calculation; Mathlib K-injectivity of extended nonnegative injective complexes.

proof.text: Use Mathlib InjectiveResolution.desc and desc_commutes for the lift of u. Mathlib InjectiveResolution.descHomotopy gives a homotopy between any two such lifts directly, so the more general uniqueness-into-injectives lemma is unnecessary.

Write $F_n=(fv_n)_*v_n^*$ and $T_V(t)^{n,q}=F_n(t^q)$. The coherent model makes each $F_n$ additive and every coface restriction a natural transformation in the module. Consequently $T_V(t)$ commutes with both differentials. On each finite diagonal its direct sum is a chain map $T_V(t):\operatorname{Tot}B_V(I)\to\operatorname{Tot}B_V(J)$; these maps preserve identities and composition term by term. Naturality of the localization unit gives $T_V(t)b_{V,I}=b_{V,J}f_*t$: in the $(0,q)$ summand it is precisely $F_0(t^q)f_*(\eta_{I^q})=f_*(\eta_{J^q})f_*(t^q)$, and every other summand is zero.

source.place: Tags 04IE and 04J4; agent finite-diagonal calculation from the coherent restriction model.

proof.text: Bundle the additive functors M ↦ G(E_n(M)) and their horizontal differentials as a nonnegative complex E of additive functors. Evaluate E on I using the additive bifunctor given by the forgetful functor from bundled additive functors. This bicomplex is componentwise canonically isomorphic to the specified flipped coherent bicomplex. Transport Mathlib mapBifunctorMapHomotopy₂ along the totalizations of these identity-component isomorphisms. Its summand formula is precisely (-1)^n G(E_n(s^{q+1})); its bottom row is zero because s^{0,0}=0. Extend the resulting homotopy by zero and apply Q_map_eq_of_homotopy.

proof.text: Naturality of rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ, with the unit identified as the inverse of rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso at the two K-injective resolutions, gives the naturality square for the inverses. Combine it with the naturality of mapExtendIso and the chain-lift equation I.ι ≫ t = single₀(u) ≫ I'.ι. Associativity and functoriality give comparison_naturality. Precompose the localized chain-augmentation square with the comparison to obtain the claimed alpha square.

source.place: Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective), canonical comparison on computing resolutions; naturality of the right-derived unit.

proof.text: Choose a reverse lift of the identity using InjectiveResolution.desc. The two composites and the corresponding identity maps lift the same identity. Apply descHomotopy and the signed-total homotopy above to show that their localized total maps coincide with identities. They are inverse maps, proving IsIso. Identity and composition laws are the strict functor laws of totalization and extension.

source.place: Tag 013S (lemma-morphisms-equal-up-to-homotopy); agent application to two compositions of lifts.

proof.text: For $r:V'\to V$, the maps $r_n=(r,\ldots,r):V'^{n+1}\to V^{n+1}$ commute with deleting and repeating coordinates. The coherent model assigns actual restriction transformations $E_{V_n}\to E_{V'_n}$, natural in the module, and commuting with its augmentations. Apply $f_*$ in every resolution degree. This produces a bicomplex map, hence a total chain map $\rho_r$. On the $(0,q)$ summand augmentation compatibility is $\operatorname{res}_{r_0}\eta_{V,I^q}=\eta_{V',I^q}$, so $\rho_rb_{V,I}=b_{V',I}$. Multiplying its localized equality by $e_I^{-1}$ gives $Q(\rho_r)\alpha_{V,K,I}=\alpha_{V',K,I}$.

source.place: Tag 04J4 (lemma-relocalize-ringed-topos); actual nerve restrictions and the coherent-model unit compatibility.

proof.text: Restrictions for the identity are identities and restrictions for a composite are composites, because $A\mapsto E_A$ is a contravariant functor. Thus the same is true of $\rho$ after finite-diagonal summation. For a lift $t$, naturality of $E_{V_n}\to E_{V'_n}$ at the module map $t^q$ reads $\operatorname{res}_{r_n}F_n(t^q)=F'_n(t^q)\operatorname{res}_{r_n}$. Summing gives $\rho_r T_V(t)=T_{V'}(t)\rho_r$. These equalities remain equalities after $Q$, and lift independence from step 4 makes them compatible with every resolution comparison.

source.place: Tag 04J4 (lemma-relocalize-ringed-topos); functoriality and naturality of actual restrictions.

proof.text: For every nonnegative bicomplex, define the degree-k projection by totalDesc, identity on its (0,k) summand and zero on all other summands. Verify the chain-map equation on each summand: the horizontal differential raises the first index, so its projected part vanishes; the vertical part has sign 1 at first index zero and projects to zero elsewhere. Apply this to the coherent bicomplex. The prescribed augmentation components give b ≫ projection = columnUnit. D.unit gives both the identification with the ordinary adjunction unit and its identity transpose, and the ordinary adjunction triangle gives the termwise counit normalization.

source.place: Tag 04IE (lemma-localize-ringed-topos); derived.tex Tag 08BJ, termwise adjunction on homotopy categories.

proof.text: Use the element-module extension adjunction to see that slice pullback is also a right adjoint. Together with D.adj this gives exactness and additivity. The element module category is Grothendieck abelian by the ring-sheaves Grothendieck theorem; the source Grothendieck K-injective theorem gives unbounded K-injective resolutions. For any additive functor, quasi-isomorphisms between K-injectives are homotopy equivalences (Mathlib), hence the mapped Q functor inverts them. The K-injective localizer therefore proves that rightDerivedFunctor with rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ is right-derived directly on complexes. Since slice pullback is exact, mapDerivedCategory and its right-derived whiskering are left-derived by the inversion criterion. Its whiskering with the right-derived functor is right-derived by the same K-injective criterion. Apply Mathlib Adjunction.derived to the ordinary termwise adjunction, and use derivedη_fac_app and derivedε_fac_app to obtain the Hom, unit, and counit formulas. The triangle is the derived adjunction triangle. Finally element_module_presheaf_extension proves that extension by zero is left exact. Its right adjoint, slice pullback, therefore preserves injectives. The restricted nonnegative injective resolution extends to a K-injective complex; transport this along mapExtendIso. The separate resolving-derived-adjunction theorem, arbitrary-universe commutative-ring resolution theorem, and Cech injective-column theorem are not needed.

Read in full against every cited statement. Steps 1-3: the slice-adjunction lemma (small element site, exact j^*, relocalization along B→A) and the column model (existence of the coherent model, K-injectivity of I and v_n^*I, comparisons from the right-derived units) supply the setup. Lift existence (h=u) and lift uniqueness (α=a, bounded-below injective target J, t0a=t1a) have all their hypotheses. Strict functoriality comes from the contravariant E_A functor and the natural unit. Steps 4-6, redone by hand: H=(-1)^nF_n(s) gives the vertical part F(ds+sd), and the horizontal part (-1)^n[d_hF_n(s)-F_{n+1}(s)d_h] vanishes by coface naturality; q=0 maps into J^{-1}=0. e_I=Rf_*(Qa)^{-1}δ_I with naturality of δ gives e_JQ(f_*t)=Rf_*(u[0])e_I. Inverse comparisons come from uniqueness plus step 4. Steps 7-8: refinement squares, identity and composition follow from the coherent model's natural restrictions that commute with the augmentation. Steps 9-10: the coherent model's identity transpose and the termwise counit are used; the resolving-normalization lemma is applied with G=v^* (exact, so P=K(A)), and B=Mod(X/V0) has K-injective resolutions by prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist since the element site is small. The transpose of id is Q(η_I)δ, and the transpose of Q(ε) is δ, invertible because v^*I is K-injective. Statement edits are named in the report and do not weaken anything. The old degree-zero transpose was applied to a map on Y and did not typecheck; it is now taken of η_I on X before f_*, with the column-zero projection checked to be a chain map (d_h raises the Cech degree). The epimorphism hypothesis on V' was already implicit in α_{V'}. The parent's step 4 is still served. The Stacks tags 013S/070I/070J/08BJ/09T5/0FND/04IE/04J4/07A6 exist with the cited labels; there is no SGA citation.
